anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: The costing inputs that drive plan selection (row counts, histograms, correlation, etc.) are stale or incomplete, causing systematic cardinality misestimation.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: Aggregate buffer cache, work-area, and auxiliary memory growth pushes the host into sustained pressure, paging, or OOM scenarios.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: The physical disks or storage fabric are saturated in IOPS, bandwidth, or latency, so read/write requests queue and slow down regardless of database intent.

When all three conditions coexist, the workload experiences erratic and worsening performance: queries are compiled into sub-optimal plans that favor either hash joins, large sorts, or table scans based on bad statistics, which in turn allocate excessive work memory and drive up buffer-cache churn. The inflated memory footprint exhausts physical RAM, causing the kernel to start paging exactly while the storage subsystem is already operating at or beyond its throughput limits. Swapping competes with normal data, temp, and log I/O, so I/O queues back up even further. Execution plans then encounter both severe memory pressure (work-area spills, frequent eviction of hot pages) and disk stalls (elevated read/write latency), leading to unstable runtimes, timeouts, and possible instance crashes.

Causally, stale or missing statistics mislead the optimizer into choosing data-hungry execution strategies (e.g., full scans, multi-gigabyte sorts) that inflate memory requests. These oversized allocations accelerate consumption of buffer cache and per-query work memory, tipping the system into OS-level paging. The resulting swap traffic lands on already saturated storage, deepening I/O queues and latency. Conversely, high I/O latency slows down statistics collection jobs, prolonging staleness and reinforcing bad plans, while memory pressure can evict cached statistics objects, further degrading estimation accuracy. The feedback loop among poor statistics, runaway memory usage, and storage saturation drives a spiral of degrading performance across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
